title: A New Test to Predict Treatment Effectiveness in Acromegaly Patients Using Short-Acting Pasireotide
official: Development of a Short-Acting GH Suppression Test with subcutaneous short action Pasireotide (PAT) for Predicting Long-Term Response to Pasireotide LAR in Patients with Acromegaly
summary: Main objective: To develop an acute GH suppression test with pasireotide LIAM -subcutaneous short acting pasireotide- (PAT) that yields cutoff values for identifying complete response, lack of response, and intermediate response to pasireotide LAR (Signifor®).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient diagnosed with acromegaly
2. Age between 18 and 85 years
3. Patient who has undergone prior neurosurgical treatment without achieving remission after surgery and/or patient who has received treatment with first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands (fg SRLs) without achieving adequate hormonal control, as demonstrated by the absence of IGF-1 normalization after at least 6 months of full-dose therapy
4. Patient who has been or is currently treated with pasireotide (Signifor®) LAR either as monotherapy or in combination with pegvisomant and/or cabergoline or both, or after failure to respond to pasireotide is treated with pegvisomant and/or cabergoline, and has shown one of the following responses: · Complete response · Partial response (IGF-1 reduction >50% without achieving normalization of IGF-1) · Incomplete response (IGF-1 reduction <50%)
5. Post-menopausal women or women of childbearing potential (WOCBP), defined as women who have experienced menarche and have not achieved post-menopausal status or permanent sterility, who agree to avoid pregnancy during the study. Sexually active WOCBP must use a highly effective method of contraception (hormonal contraception, intra-uterine device (IUD), or anatomical sterility in self or partner*) while on study treatment. All female volunteers must be willing to undergo urine pregnancy tests on the day of treatment and prior to each administration of subcutaneous pasireotide (PAT1 and PAT2).
6. Having understood the information provided and capable of giving consent to participate in this trial by signing the Informed Consent document
Exclusion criteria:
1. Renal insufficiency, defined as a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) < 40 mL/min.
2. Patients with hepatic cirrhosis, including severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C).
3. Patients with oncologic diseases currently receiving active treatment
4. Patients with undernutrition, defined as BMI<17.
5. Patients with diabetes mellitus and poor metabolic control (A1c > 9%).
6. Pregnant women, those actively seeking pregnancy, or those who are breastfeeding at the time of enrollment
7. Severe psychiatric disorders
8. To participate in other clinical studies involving drugs for acromegaly.
9. Patients with a history of serious adverse reactions or hypersensitivity to pasireotide.
